issues.summary: Refine: scientists want concept-set save errors to say which name clashed
issues.description:
Raw request from the R&D epidemiology group: when a concept set save fails because the name is taken, the error should say which name clashed.
Today the message is generic, so scientists guess, rename and retry, and some file support tickets instead.

Request as received (not yet refined):
"When I save a concept set and it already exists, tell me the name it clashed with, and ideally the ID of the other set so I can open it."

Open questions:
- Does this apply to cohort definitions too, or concept sets only?
- Is the clash case-sensitive?
- Should the message show the other set's ID and owner, given some sets are private to a team?

Acceptance criteria (draft, incomplete):
AC1 Saving a concept set whose name already exists returns 409 with a message that names the clashing concept set.
AC2 The message contains no raw database text.
AC3 TBD after refinement: cohort definitions, case handling, what the message may disclose about the other set.

issues.summary: ConceptSetService: return the clashing name in the 409 on duplicate concept-set save
issues.description:
Implement the refined duplicate-name message for concept-set create and update in ConceptSetService.
This is the developer half of the scientists' request; it builds on the safe 409 from GSK-1 and must not reintroduce raw database text.

Starts after the refinement story is complete and its acceptance criteria are agreed.

Acceptance criteria:
AC1 POST /conceptset/ and PUT /conceptset/{id} with a name already in use return 409 and a message naming the clashing concept set.
AC2 The check uses the existing conceptSetExists query, not the database constraint text.
AC3 Unit tests cover create, update to an existing name and update keeping its own name.
AC4 build, tests and scan checks green; PR fills Ticket, URS delta, Test mapping and Change record sections.

issues.summary: Test design: OQ cases for GenericExceptionMapper error responses
issues.description:
Write the operational qualification (OQ) test cases that prove GenericExceptionMapper returns the right status and a safe body for each exception type.
The GSK-1 fix changes what users see on errors, so the evidence pack needs test cases that trace to each acceptance criterion.

Scope: DataIntegrityViolationException (no cause, one cause, nested cause with and without 'Detail:'), and the existing 403, 404, 400, 501 and 500 mappings.

Acceptance criteria:
AC1 One OQ case per GSK-1 acceptance criterion AC1-AC5, each with input, expected status, expected body rule and pass/fail rule.
AC2 Each case names the automated test method that executes it.
AC3 Cases are added as rows to validation/traceability.csv on the GSK-1 PR branch, with reviewer and result columns left blank.
AC4 Cases run under ./reproduce.sh or mvn test without manual steps.

issues.summary: Risk assessment for GSK-1 change (CSA medium)
issues.description:
Record the risk-based (CSA) assessment for the GSK-1 error-mapper change and confirm it is medium risk, not high.
The rating decides the assurance level: medium means unscripted plus targeted scripted testing; high would mean full GAMP 5 IQ/OQ/PQ.

Acceptance criteria:
AC1 Intended use, failure modes and impact on patient safety, product quality and data integrity are written down for the change.
AC2 Rating is justified against the silver-tier criteria in validation/README.md.
AC3 Assurance activities are listed (automated regression tests, OQ cases, scientist UAT) with the evidence each produces.
AC4 Draft is attached to the change record; the approver, decision and date fields are left blank for the named GSK approver.
issues.comment: Draft is in progress. Leaning medium: the change only alters error responses, no stored data changes. Waiting on the OQ case list before writing the assurance section.

issues.summary: Security Swarm scan profile for WebAPI (authn/authz, injection)
issues.description:
Define the Security Swarm scan profile used on every WebAPI PR, focused on authentication, authorisation and injection.
Generic scanners miss Shiro filter-chain gaps and string-built SQL in WebAPI, which are the issues AppSec actually cares about here.

Scope: Shiro filter chain and permission checks on Jersey resources, JWT handling, SqlRender and JdbcTemplate query building, path and query parameter handling.

Acceptance criteria:
AC1 Profile lists the rule sets, the paths in scope and the paths excluded, with a reason for each exclusion.
AC2 Findings are rated with the existing severity rubric and map to Jira priority.
AC3 A trial run on main is attached with false positives marked and explained.
AC4 Profile runs alongside the existing scan check and does not replace it.
issues.comment: Profile draft is up for review with AppSec. Trial run on main: 14 findings, 9 marked false positive (parameterised SqlRender calls). Remaining 5 are permission checks on legacy endpoints.

issues.summary: On-call: p95 latency alert on /WebAPI/cohortdefinition after deploy
issues.description:
After the last WebAPI deploy, p95 latency on GET /WebAPI/cohortdefinition went from about 400 ms to over 3 s and paged on-call.
The cohort list is the ATLAS landing page for most scientists, so a slow list looks like ATLAS is down.

Alert text:
[FIRING] WebAPI p95 latency high: route=/WebAPI/cohortdefinition method=GET p95=3.4s threshold=1.5s for=10m env=prod

Steps to reproduce:
1. On a staging copy with production data volume (about 6,000 cohort definitions), deploy the current build.
2. Call GET /WebAPI/cohortdefinition 50 times with a normal user token.
3. Compare p95 with the previous build on the same data: previous about 0.4 s, current about 3 s.
4. Check the Grafana WebAPI dashboard: Hikari active connections stay normal, request time rises on this route only.

Acceptance criteria:
AC1 Cause identified and written on this ticket with evidence (query plan, profiler output or diff).
AC2 p95 on GET /WebAPI/cohortdefinition back under 1.5 s on the staging copy.
AC3 A regression check for the list endpoint latency is added to the release checklist.
AC4 Post-incident note drafted; no blame, owner fields left for the on-call lead.
issues.comment: Reproduced on staging. Time is spent after the query returns: each row now loads tags and permissions one by one. Checking which commit added the per-row lookups.

issues.summary: Runbook update for the Hikari pool exhaustion alert
issues.description:
Update the on-call runbook for the 'Hikari pending connections > 0 for 5 minutes' alert.
The current runbook says 'restart WebAPI', which hides the cause and drops running generations.

Acceptance criteria:
AC1 Runbook shows how to read active, idle and pending connections from the Grafana WebAPI dashboard and JMX.
AC2 Lists known causes (cancelled executions holding connections, long cohort generations, slow source database) and how to tell them apart.
AC3 Restart is the last step, with what to capture before restarting (thread dump, pool metrics).
AC4 Runbook is linked from the alert annotation.

A scientist runs user acceptance testing (PQ) of the new duplicate-name message in ATLAS on the validation environment.
This confirms the change works for the people who asked for it, in their normal workflow, not just in automated tests.

Acceptance criteria:
AC1 Scripted steps: create a concept set, create a second with the same name, read the message, rename and save.
AC2 The message names the clashing concept set and is understandable without help.
AC3 Scientist records pass/fail and any comment per step; tester name, signature and date left for the scientist.
AC4 Any failure is raised as a new bug linked to this ticket.

issues.summary: S/4 custom-code readiness inventory for abap2xlsx
issues.description:

issues.summary: ADR: Spring Boot 1.5 to 2.7 upgrade path for WebAPI
issues.description:
Write an architecture decision record (ADR) for how WebAPI moves from Spring Boot 1.5 to 2.7: one step or staged, and in what order.
The upgrade touches Jersey, Shiro, Flyway, Hikari and Java 11 at once; without an agreed path, teams make conflicting changes.

Acceptance criteria:
AC1 Options compared: single jump to 2.7, staged via 2.0/2.3, or stay on 1.5 with backported fixes; each with risk, effort and validation impact.
AC2 Recommended order for Flyway, Shiro, Jersey and Java 11 changes, with dependencies stated.
AC3 Validation impact stated per option (CSA rating, expected IQ/OQ/PQ scope).
AC4 ADR status left as Proposed; decision and approver fields left for the named architect.

issues.summary: Inspection-readiness pack for one change, end to end
issues.description:
Assemble one change (GSK-1) end to end as an inspector would ask for it: request, risk, code, tests, approvals and release.
Inspectors pick a single change and follow it; this shows whether the trail holds together without someone explaining it in the room.

Acceptance criteria:
AC1 One index page links, in order: ticket, risk assessment, URS delta, PR and commits, test results, QA review, change record, release pack.
AC2 Each link is checked to open and to refer to the same change ID.
AC3 Gaps are listed as findings, not filled in.
AC4 Who-did-what-when is shown from system records (Jira history, Git log, CI runs), not retyped.
